name: Kannayiramudayar Temple, Thirukaravasal
deity: Shiva as Kannayiramudayar, with the Thyagaraja processional deity Adhi Vidangar
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam sung in the Tevaram; the stone temple of the Chola age
summary: At Thirukaravasal in the heart of the Kaveri delta, Shiva stands as Kannayiramudayar, and the Thyagaraja of the shrine — Adhi Vidangar, the first of the Vidangas — is one of the seven dancing Thyagarajas of the delta, whose procession is said to move in the Kukkuta Natanam.

sections.history: Thirukaravasal lies among the wet fields of the Kaveri delta, near the delta's southern channels. Its temple to Shiva as Kannayiramudayar is a Paadal Petra Sthalam of Tevaram antiquity, its stone shrines carried forward under the Cholas. The temple is one of the Sapta Vidanga Sthalams, and its Thyagaraja is honoured as Adhi Vidangar, the first of the seven Vidangas of the dancing tradition.
sections.architecture: The temple is built in the Dravidian manner, its sanctum holding Shiva as Kannayiramudayar, with the Somaskanda Thyagaraja — Shiva with Uma and the child Skanda — worshipped as the uncarved Vidanga image and carried as the processional lord. Pillared halls open before the sanctum in the quiet delta manner of the Chola and later ages.
sections.legends: The Sapta Vidanga temples share the legend of the uncarved Thyagaraja images, given by the lord and worshipped in the Somaskanda form, each dancing its own dance in procession. At Thirukaravasal the Thyagaraja is Adhi Vidangar, held to be the first of the seven, and his procession is said to move in the Kukkuta Natanam, the dance likened to the strutting of a cockerel.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the festivals of Shiva and the processions of the Vidangar through the year, with the days of the Nayanmar saints and the delta's festival calendar observed in the village shrine. The procession of the dancing Thyagaraja is the heart of its celebration.
sections.experience: Thirukaravasal is a quiet delta shrine off the main pilgrim roads, rewarding for the devotee who follows the seven dancing Thyagarajas from one delta town to the next. It lies within the cluster of Vidanga temples between Thiruvarur and the coast, and joins them into the single pilgrimage of the seven dances.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; festival days and processions are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Men are traditionally asked to remove the upper garment before the sanctum, as at many southern shrines; follow the posted rules.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirukaravasal lies in the Kaveri delta in the Thiruvarur–Nagapattinam country, reached by road from Thiruvarur and the surrounding delta towns.
